chunk_findings.detail: `is_dir` cannot see root or current-directory roots because it only checks `d in self.dirs` or `f.startswith(d + "/")`. For `.` this never matches keys such as `a.txt`; for `/` it tests the prefix `//` and never matches `/a.txt`. Input: `FakeFs({"a.txt": b"x"}).copy_tree(".", "dst")` raises `FileNotFoundError`, and `FakeFs({"/a.txt": b"x"}).copy_tree("/", "/dst")` raises `FileNotFoundError`; real `shutil.copytree` would copy the contents.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:is_dir

chunk_findings.detail: `move` does not implement the real `shutil.move` rule that an existing directory destination means “put the source inside that directory”. Input: `fs = FakeFs({"src.txt": b"x"}); fs.mkdir("dst"); fs.move("src.txt", "dst")` ends with `fs.files == {"dst": b"x"}`, making `dst` a file instead of `dst/src.txt`. A directory source into an existing directory likewise merges contents into `dst` rather than creating `dst/<name>`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:move

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_tree` fails to reject an existing file destination. Input: `fs = FakeFs({"dst": b"x", "src/a.txt": b"y"}); fs.mkdir("src"); fs.copy_tree("src", "dst")` does not raise `FileExistsError`; it adds `dst/a.txt` while leaving `dst` as a file, producing an impossible state. Real `shutil.copytree` rejects an existing non-directory destination even with `dirs_exist_ok=True`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:copy_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `_under('/')` computes `root + "/"` = `"//"`, and `is_dir` uses the same `d + "/"` prefix. A `FakeFs` containing `{'/a': b'x'}` returns `False` for `is_dir('/')`, and `copy_tree('/', '/dst')` copies no files, while `rmtree('/', ignore_errors=False)` raises `FileNotFoundError` for an existing root. The root directory is a valid path and must be considered a directory when it has children.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:_under

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_tree` copies only `self.files` and adds only `dst` to `self.dirs`; it never copies descendant directories. Input `fs=FakeFs(); fs.mkdir('/src'); fs.mkdir('/src/empty'); fs.copy_tree('/src','/dst')` leaves `fs.is_dir('/dst/empty') == False`, whereas `shutil.copytree` preserves empty subdirectories. The fake therefore does not mirror the real operation for valid directory trees.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:copy_tree

chunk_findings.detail: When moving a directory, `move` relocates only files beneath it and then does `self.dirs.discard(s); self.dirs.add(d)`, so descendant `dirs` entries of `s` are left behind. Input `fs=FakeFs(); fs.mkdir('/a'); fs.mkdir('/a/b'); fs.files['/a/b/f']=b'x'; fs.move('/a','/c')` leaves `fs.is_dir('/a/b') == True`. Real `shutil.move` removes the source tree, so this fake state is wrong and can make later tests pass under a moved-away path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:move

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_tree` only rejects an existing destination when `self.is_dir(d)` is true. If `d` already exists as a file and `dirs_exist_ok=False`, it does not raise. Input `fs=FakeFs({'/src/f': b's', '/dst': b'old'}); fs.copy_tree('/src','/dst')` instead creates `/dst/f` and adds `/dst` to dirs, leaving `/dst` as both a file and directory. `shutil.copytree` raises `FileExistsError` for an existing file destination.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:copy_tree

chunk_findings.detail: `ddflow/adapters/fs.py` adds `Fs.replace_path`, and its docstring says callers reach the path operations through `ddflow.infra.fsio`. But the `fsio` hunk only routes `copy_file`, `copy_tree`, `move`, and `rmtree` through `_fs.DEFAULT`; there is no `replace_path` wrapper. A caller following the stated contract and doing `from ddflow.infra.fsio import replace_path` gets `ImportError`, and the atomic-replace path is never routed through the fake/default adapter, so that part of the new contract is not actually wired.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/fsio.py

chunk_findings.detail: [r-adapters] The `os_replace` allowed-home set now contains both `ddflow.infra.fsio` and `ddflow.adapters.fs`. r-adapters requires one implementation per function in `ddflow/adapters`; keeping `ddflow.infra.fsio` as an allowed home alongside the new `Fs` port preserves a second direct `os.replace` call site (atomic text writes in `infra.fsio`) outside the adapter, so a `FakeFs`/swap cannot govern all atomic replacement behavior. This also conflicts with the operator decision that the home is `ddflow/adapters/`, not `ddflow/infra`.

chunk_findings.detail: `move('/file', '/dir')` where `/dir` is an existing directory is wrong: `self.files[d] = self.files.pop(s)` stores the file at the exact key `/dir` instead of `/dir/file`. Real `shutil.move` moves a file *into* an existing directory, so this fake leaves `/dir` represented both as a directory and as a file, making later `is_dir`/read/write behavior inconsistent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:FakeFs.move

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_tree('/src', '/dst')` does not copy empty directories. If `/src/empty` was created with `mkdir`, only `self.dirs.add(d)` is called, so `is_dir('/dst/empty')` returns `False`. Real `shutil.copytree` copies empty directories, so the fake silently loses directory structure for callers that use empty dirs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:FakeFs.copy_tree

chunk_findings.detail: When `dst` exists as a file and `dirs_exist_ok` is left at its default `False`, a real `shutil.copytree('/src', '/dst')` raises `FileExistsError`. This fake checks only `self.is_dir(d)` and therefore proceeds to write files under `/dst/...`, creating a file path that simultaneously acts as a directory prefix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:FakeFs.copy_tree

chunk_findings.detail: For the root path `/`, `d + "/"` becomes `"//"`, so a file under root such as `/a` does not satisfy `f.startswith("//")`. Thus `FakeFs(files={'/a': b'x'}).is_dir('/')` returns `False` even though the class docstring says a directory exists when a file lies under it. As a result `copy_tree`, `move`, or `rmtree` on root fails or loses entries.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:FakeFs.is_dir

chunk_findings.detail: The class docstring states `calls` records every operation as `(name, *paths)`, but `mkdir` mutates `self.dirs` without appending to `self.calls`. A test or caller relying on `calls` to observe directory creation will not see it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:FakeFs.mkdir

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds `Fs.replace_path` in `ddflow/adapters/fs.py` and the intent says atomic replace extends the `ddflow.infra.fsio` home, with `Fs`’s own docstring saying callers reach it through `ddflow.infra.fsio`. But `ddflow/infra/fsio.py` only adds/rewraps `copy_file`, `copy_tree`, `move`, and `rmtree`; there is no `replace_path` wrapper or re-export. A caller following the documented path, `from ddflow.infra.fsio import replace_path`, gets `ImportError`, so atomic replace is not actually available through the fsio caller home.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/fsio.py

chunk_findings.detail: The `os_replace` allowed-homes set is changed to include both `ddflow.infra.fsio` and `ddflow.adapters.fs`. This violates the operator decision that the filesystem home is `ddflow/adapters/` (not `ddflow/infra`) and [r-adapters]: `os.replace` is a filesystem primitive that must be reached through the Fs port in `ddflow.adapters.fs`. Keeping `ddflow.infra.fsio` in the allowed set means a direct `os.replace(src, dst)` in `ddflow.infra.fsio` still passes the architecture guard, bypassing `Fs.replace_path`. The old home should be removed rather than retained alongside the new adapter.

chunk_findings.detail: The one-adapter wiring test never calls `fsio.replace_path`. It calls `fsio.copy_file`, `fsio.copy_tree`, `fsio.move`, and `fsio.rmtree` under a patched `F.DEFAULT` fake, then asserts only those four call names. A defective implementation where `fsio.replace_path` directly calls `os.replace` or `shutil.move` (bypassing `F.DEFAULT`) would still produce exactly `["copy_file", "copy_tree", "move", "rmtree"]` and pass, so the atomic-replace part of the new fsio contract is not enforced by this test.
